findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, giving it a public endpoint reachable from the internet. Combined with an admin user and a shared password variable, this greatly expands attack surface for the catalog database.
storage_encrypted = false disables KMS encryption of the RDS volume, snapshots and backups, leaving stored data in cleartext on disk.

The master password is supplied from var.password and is also interpolated into EC2 user_data; no secrets manager is used, so the plaintext credential is persisted in Terraform state and rendered into instance metadata.

findings.issue_category: no enforced TLS for DB connections
findings.description: The parameter group applied contains no require_secure_transport setting and the PHP client connects with mysqli_connect without TLS options, so database traffic including credentials can travel unencrypted.

The database password, username and endpoint are written into the instance user_data script, which is readable in plaintext by anyone with access to the instance metadata service (169.254.169.254/latest/user-data) or EC2 DescribeInstanceAttribute permission.

No root_block_device/ebs encryption is configured, so the instance volume - which stores the dbinfo.inc file containing the database password - is likely unencrypted at rest depending on AMI defaults.

No metadata_options block requires IMDSv2 (http_tokens = "required"), so the instance credentials from the over-privileged instance profile and the user_data secrets can be retrieved via SSRF against the metadata endpoint.

The instance is deployed in a subnet and its public_dns is exported as an output, indicating it receives a public IP; it serves an unauthenticated PHP page over plaintext HTTP only (httpd with no TLS), transmitting submitted employee data in the clear.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*". Attached to a role assumed by an internet-facing EC2 instance, compromise of the web application yields near-total control of S3 data, EC2 and RDS in the account, including privilege escalation paths.
The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, enabling data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database host.
Port 3306 is opened to the entire VPC CIDR rather than only the application server's security group, so any workload in the VPC can reach the database directly.
